topic: Trusting useful AI answers while only partly understanding how they are produced.
audience: Professionals curious about how AI changes everyday work and judgment; no specialist knowledge assumed.
objective: Explore why a convincing AI answer and a sound reason to rely on it are different questions. Use the deliberately prepared structure; keep Graham curious, measured and broad, with no technical credentials or invented experience.

evidence.title: ANTHROPIC-2025
evidence.fact: In its March 2025 interpretability report, Anthropic traced parts of Claude 3.5 Haiku’s internal computations and explicitly said its method captured only a fraction of the total computation, even on short prompts.

evidence.title: BUCINCA-2021
evidence.fact: In a 199-participant AI-assisted decision-making experiment, interventions encouraging deliberate engagement reduced overreliance more than the simple explanation approaches tested; participants rated the most effective interventions less favorably.

meaning.reader_consequence: Consider what would justify reliance when a fluent explanation is easier to get than understanding.

facts.text: In its March 2025 interpretability report, Anthropic traced parts of Claude 3.5 Haiku’s internal computations and explicitly said its method captured only a fraction of the total computation, even on short prompts.

In a 199-participant AI-assisted decision-making experiment, interventions encouraging deliberate engagement reduced overreliance more than the simple explanation approaches tested; participants rated the most effective interventions less favorably.

meaning.qualification: Partial interpretability is not total ignorance. The controlled decision-support experiment predates current chatbots; explanations can help in some conditions. Do not universalize trust, overreliance or opaque systems.

beats: Tension: develop why the question matters.
Evidence: place the relevant sourced facts.
Interpretation: develop Graham's reading and its limits.
Landing: earn the closing thought from the argument.
